title: records copied from one original count once
line: the state's own death index line and FamilySearch's index of the same death are two copies of one death certificate: once the owner accepts FamilySearch's entry, the line agrees with the tree on the day of the death and on the age, but the tree holds both only from that certificate, so neither is a point and the rule leaves the line to the owner, saying why

steps.say: his Kentucky death index entry on FamilySearch, which the file cites: died 11 Jun 1946
the owner accepts it as his: the 11th against the file's 10th, which the rule decides for the record of the death
the same death as the line of the state's own index file holds it, Reclaim the Records' copy

expect.why: the line agrees with the tree to the day, but on nothing the tree holds from any other record: a card for the owner

has: the death date, which the tree holds only from the death certificate, the original this record was copied from

expect.why: both indexes copy one certificate: FamilySearch's entry, primary information on the death, is no corroboration of its own copy
